original_question: How do recurrences in a dynamical system, including periodic orbits and more general recurrent structures either near the hole or elsewhere in phase space, affect escape for systems with little or no hyperbolicity?
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s actual target. It correctly identifies recurrence as the central theme, explicitly includes periodic orbits together with more general recurrent behaviour, preserves the paper’s distinction between recurrence near the hole and recurrence elsewhere in phase space, and keeps the intended low-/non-hyperbolic regime.
missing_details: The paper’s setting is an open system with a hole H⊂Ω and dynamics Φ^t, not just an arbitrary dynamical system in the abstract.
The escape problem is formulated via the surviving set Ω_t={x∈Ω: Φ^s(x)∉H for all s∈(0,t]} and the survival probability P(t)=μ0(Ω_t) for an initial probability measure μ0 at time 0.
The official problem asks for a general description of the effect of recurrence on escape, rather than a specific asymptotic formula, optimization rule, or escape-rate theorem.

The nearby discussion explains the relevance of periodic orbits especially for initial measures supported away from the hole, since such orbits and their neighborhoods often control the non-escaping set and long-time survival behaviour.
The paper explicitly treats recurrence more broadly than periodic orbits: in finite billiards without periodic orbits, analogous return behaviour is still linked to Poincaré recurrence.
The spatial qualifier should be kept exact: the recurrence may matter in the vicinity of the hole and/or elsewhere in phase space.
The intended scope is the poorly understood little-/non-hyperbolic regime, contrasted with the substantial existing theory for hyperbolic systems.
Not applicable here: there are no ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency conditions; the needed formal data are dynamical (Ω, H, Φ^t, μ0, Ω_t, P(t)).
refined_question: In the open-system setting of the paper, with phase space Ω, hole H⊂Ω, dynamics Φ^t, surviving set Ω_t={x∈Ω: Φ^s(x)∉H for all s∈(0,t]}, and survival probability P(t)=μ0(Ω_t) for an initial measure μ0, give a general description of how recurrences of the underlying dynamics—periodic orbits and more general recurrent behaviour—affect the escape problem, both when those recurrences occur near the hole H and when they occur elsewhere in phase space, in systems with little or no hyperbolicity.
justification: The draft is nearest to Problem 11.18 in §11.6, whose wording and scope it nearly matches. To make the question stand-alone, one must import the §11.3 open-system notation defining the hole H, surviving set Ω_t, and survival probability P(t)=μ0(Ω_t). The nearby §11.6 discussion explains why periodic orbits and their neighborhoods matter for long-time survival, notes that similar return behaviour persists even without periodic orbits via recurrence, and places the problem explicitly in the low-/non-hyperbolic regime. Earlier recurrence-focused problems—hole placement relative to short periodic orbits (Problem 11.3), polygonal survival governed by neighborhoods of non-escaping periodic orbits (Problem 11.7), marginally unstable periodic orbits in stadium-like billiards (Problem 11.9), and sticky mixed billiards (Problem 11.10)—are concrete precursors that §11.6 is synthesizing, rather than a different broader target.
